schoolPressures.label: Harvest labour
schoolPressures.detail: Economic pressure can pull girls into farm labour during coffee harvest, when every extra pair of hands matters.

schoolPressures.label: Monsoon roads
schoolPressures.detail: His daughter's bus becomes unreliable when hill roads wash out in the heavy monsoon months.

schoolPressures.label: Girls' mobility
schoolPressures.detail: Concern over girls' mobility and perceived sexual purity grows once they reach adolescence.

schoolPressures.label: Protest bandhs
schoolPressures.detail: Sringeri's ESA bandh shut shops, banks and schools for a day, a land-rights disruption to schooling.

pressures: Coffee harvest is when every pair of hands counts, so economic pressure can pull his 14-year-old daughter into estate work during those weeks.
When hill roads wash out in heavy monsoon months, her bus becomes unreliable, and a few lost weeks make it harder for her to keep up.
As she reaches adolescence, concern over girls' mobility grows, which can weigh against sending her far for the next stage.
Sringeri's ESA bandh shut schools for a day, so land-rights disputes in the hills can cost his children school days.
factorEffects.sanitation: If his estate home lacked a proper toilet, his 14-year-old daughter's attendance would suffer first; the card gives no sign this is his family's problem.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Chikkamagaluru. The card shows harvest labour, monsoon roads, girls' mobility and bandhs as the pressures, not language.

changes.effect: Many of Chikkamagaluru's classrooms need repair; in the heavy monsoon a leaking room can stop lessons for his daughter, 14, in Class 9.

changes.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
changes.effect: Most homes in the district have a toilet; if any did not, it is daughters like his who would face the safety and privacy worries first.
Sport and a playground give adolescents a reason to stay on; for his daughter, school has to outweigh the pull of harvest labour.

lag.effect: Few schools here have a protected well; where a school has no other safe source, drinking water is not assured through the monsoon and the dry months.

schoolPressures.label: Limited village school
schoolPressures.detail: The family judged village school options beyond middle school too limited for the higher secondary years.

schoolPressures.label: Landslide roads
schoolPressures.detail: The daily commute on Kodagu's landslide-prone roads was judged too unreliable to sustain.

schoolPressures.label: Hostel costs
schoolPressures.detail: Families in remoter estate hamlets say they cannot always afford to place a child in a hostel.

schoolPressures.label: Flood disruption
schoolPressures.detail: A single monsoon season can knock a rural Kodagu child's schooling off track for a year or more.

pressures: Her village school's options beyond middle school are limited, so keeping her daughter in school means boarding in Madikeri, and that is the pressure.
Landslide-prone roads made the daily commute unreliable, so boarding or leaving becomes the only choice.
Remote estate hamlets say hostel costs are not always affordable, so which child gets the seat can become a family decision.
A single monsoon season can knock her child's schooling off track for a year or more, so one flood can cost a grade.
factorEffects.sanitation: If her estate home lacked a proper toilet, her children's attendance would be affected; the card gives no sign this is her family's problem.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Kodagu. The card shows limited village schooling, landslide roads, hostel costs and floods as the pressures, not language.

changes.effect: Kodagu already has many women teachers; for her daughter, 15, boarding in Madikeri, that can make secondary school feel safer.
Safe classrooms matter in a district where landslides and floods have disrupted schooling; repaired rooms keep lessons going after a bad monsoon.
Women in Kodagu are among the most schooled in Karnataka; like her, mothers who studied longer tend to keep their children in school.

lag.effect: Toilet coverage in Kodagu's schools is high but not complete; for her daughter, boarding in Madikeri, a working toilet at school matters every day.
